operations.title: Research state for BSSC private-message sum-capacity
operations.summary: For the stated binary-input broadcast channel, the exact private-message sum-capacity remains open. The governed benchmark is 0.361642884421954615663441578150587… ≤ C_sum ≤ 0.369296945969202842443. The upper endpoint is a certified universal converse from a continuous full-Theorem-9 calculation at one fixed reflected binary auxiliary-receiver pair. It does not establish matching achievability, global optimality of the pair or dual face, or certification of the smaller numerical lead 0.369296340638082.

operations.title: Auxiliary-receiver outer-bound program
operations.summary: This program studies the Gohari–Liu–Nair two-auxiliary-receiver outer bound through input-only structural reductions, finite-grid analysis, exact symbolic dual certificates, continuous posterior majorants, symmetry identities, and optimization over auxiliary-receiver pairs and dual choices. It includes a certified continuous fixed-pair converse C_sum ≤ 0.369296945969202842443 and an exact skew-invariant representation of its six-row functional. Global receiver cardinality, binary or reflected-pair sufficiency, invariant-dual sufficiency, global minimization, matching achievability, and the exact capacity remain unresolved, with stated source-transcription and implementation trust boundaries.

operations.title: Continuous full-Theorem-9 converse for a fixed reflected binary receiver pair
operations.summary: For the reflected binary pair G=(0.206961624915382,0.826953249115544) and K=(0.173046750884456,0.793038375084618), a continuum-wide full-Theorem-9 certificate establishes C_sum ≤ 0.369296945969202842443. The certificate uses an exact nonnegative six-row combination, posterior-functional audits, affine majorants over all posterior values in [0,1], analytic maximization over every input prior, and outward-rounded interval evaluation. It does not establish optimality of the pair or dual, global binary or reflected-pair sufficiency, matching achievability, or the smaller numerical lead.

operations.title: Exact skew-invariant representation of the frontier six-row functional
operations.summary: For every 0 ≤ epsilon ≤ 1/3, the frontier non-invariant six-row combination induces exactly the same posterior-hierarchy functional as a nonnegative skew-invariant six-row combination for every input prior, auxiliary-receiver pair, and admissible three-group hierarchy. This identity does not establish global sufficiency of invariant duals or reflected receiver pairs, or optimality of the certified pair or epsilon. Identification with the named rank-eight quotient coordinates remains conditional on the prior quotient convention.

operations.title: Bridge from local or finite auxiliary-receiver analyses to the global receiver functional
operations.summary: A continuum-wide certificate for one specified reflected binary auxiliary-receiver pair now yields the universal converse C_sum ≤ 0.369296945969202842443 without requiring a finite-grid-to-continuum theorem. The global bridge remains unresolved: no supplied result establishes continuum receiver cardinality, finite-grid convergence or infimum interchange, global binary-, reflected-pair-, or invariant-dual sufficiency, optimality of the certified pair or dual face, global minimization, certification of the smaller numerical lead, matching achievability, or the exact capacity.

operations.title: Fidelity of the Theorem 9 transcription and quotient-coordinate identification
operations.summary: Internal exact audits support the selected six-row weights, rate normalization, sparse posterior-tensor expansion, root-level cancellations, and equality of the original and skew-invariant functionals. The fixed-pair converse remains conditional on the cited Theorem 9, correct transcription of the selected rows and side-condition orientation, and documented logarithm behavior. Complete manuscript comparison remains unavailable, and the named rank-eight quotient-coordinate identification remains conditional on the prior quotient convention, although the functional identity is independently supported.
